# Model and source

```{r model, include = FALSE}
mod <- readModelDb("Lazarou_2020_pembrolizumab_qsp")
rxmod <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
mod_meta <- rxmod$meta
```

* Citation: `r mod_meta$reference`
* Description: `r mod_meta$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.1786> (open access:
  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7158209/>)
* Supporting Information (calibration narrative, virtual-trial parameter
  distributions, Figure S1 process map, and the executable model code
  `CIC_v2.2.6` as CSV documentation plus R and MATLAB exports): available from
  the article page.

Lazarou et al. (2020) is a tutorial on using clinical omics resources to
parameterise quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models in
immuno-oncology. To illustrate the approach the authors built a minimal
Cancer Immunity Cycle (CIC) model, calibrated it for non-small cell lung
carcinoma (NSCLC) treated with pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg every three weeks, and
ran a 489-patient virtual trial (main-text Figure 4). The model is explicitly
an illustration: the authors state it was not qualified for drug-development
decisions.

# Population and biological context

The model has no fitted population in the popPK sense. Its inputs come from
three kinds of data (Supplementary Information, "Minimal model calibration
using omics data"; main-text Figure 3):

* **Tumour microenvironment (TME) composition** from the Immune Landscape of
  Cancer resource, averaging lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell
  carcinoma biopsies (1156 patients): leukocyte fraction 0.14, and the relative
  cytotoxic T-cell and antigen-presenting-cell (dendritic cell + M1
  macrophage) fractions that split it into maximal TME percentages of 7.4 %
  and 6.6 %.
* **Lymph-node T cells** from healthy-donor flow cytometry, T-cell repertoire
  sequencing and the absolute lymph-node lymphocyte count of Trepel (1974).
* **Tumour-volume trajectories of four KEYNOTE-001 NSCLC patients** treated
  with pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W (three responders, one non-responder), used
  to calibrate tumour growth, T-cell killing and PD-1 checkpoint action by
  hand.

The virtual trial uses 489 virtual patients, each weighing 70 kg, given 19
doses of 10 mg/kg every 21 days over 399 days. The same information is
available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(mod_meta$population, give.attr = FALSE)
```

# Model structure

* **PK.** Pembrolizumab (nmol) enters an injection-site depot, from which a
  fraction `fdepot` is absorbed at rate `ka` and the rest is lost; a central
  compartment with linear elimination exchanges with one peripheral
  compartment. Plasma concentration is `Cc = central * mw / vblood`.
* **Tumour.** Tumour cells (`tumor`) grow logistically towards a TME capacity
  (`capacity`) that the tumour recruits at a rate inversely proportional to
  its own TME percentage; they die at a basal rate and are killed by cytotoxic
  T cells (`tc_tme`) with a saturable dependence on the TME T-cell percentage.
* **Cancer immunity cycle.** Killed tumour cells form the antigen pool
  (`antigens`), which TME antigen-presenting cells (`apc_tme`) take up and
  carry to the lymph node (`apc_ln`); lymph-node APCs drive proliferation of
  neoantigen-specific T cells (`tc_ln`), which traffic to the TME up to a
  maximal TME percentage. APCs are produced in the TME up to their own maximal
  percentage.
* **Checkpoint.** TME T cells become exhausted via PD-1 at a rate that rises
  with the tumour percentage of the TME and falls with antibody occupancy,
  `central / (central + kd_pd1)`.
* **Initial state.** The tumour starts at volume `TUM_VOL` (mm^3), already
  infiltrated to its maximal leukocyte fractions; the TME volume is the cell
  count times the volume of one cell (`vcell`).

# Source trace

Every structural equation and parameter value comes from the authors'
deposited model code (`CIC_v2.2.6`): the CSV documentation (`Parameters.csv`,
`Species.csv`, `Reactions.csv`, `Assignments.csv`, `Compartments.csv`,
`DosingPlans.csv`) and the R export (`initialiseQSP.R`, `integrateQSP.R`),
which agree with each other.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (kabs) | log(2) 1/day | Parameters.csv `kabs` |
| `lfdepot` (Fabs) | log(0.9815751) | Parameters.csv `Fabs` |
| `lkel` | log(0.07342571) 1/day | Parameters.csv `kel` |
| `lk12`, `lk21` | log(0.4), log(0.43) 1/day | Parameters.csv `k12`, `k21` |
| `mw` | 146000 g/mol | Parameters.csv `MWantiPD1` |
| `vblood` | 2.75 L | Parameters.csv `Vblood`; Assignments.csv A9 |
| `kd_pd1` | 0.076595741 nmol | Parameters.csv `antiPD1_KD` |
| `kg_tumor` (mu) | 0.4 1/day | Parameters.csv `mu`; Assignments.csv A16 |
| `kv1` | 0.01 1/day | Parameters.csv `kv1`; Assignments.csv A17 |
| `kdeath_tumor` (beta_tumor) | 0.0231 1/day | Parameters.csv `beta_tumor`; Assignments.csv A18 |
| `kkill` | 0.3 1/day | Parameters.csv `kkill`; Assignments.csv A19 |
| `pcc50_kill` (Kkill) | 3.45 % | Parameters.csv `Kkill` |
| `kexh_pd1` (kPD1) | 300 1/day | Parameters.csv `kPD1`; Assignments.csv A20 |
| `ptum50_pd1` (KPD1) | 43.5 % | Parameters.csv `KPD1` |
| `leuk_frac` | 0.14 | Parameters.csv `Leuk_frac`; Supplementary Information p. 1 |
| `tc_frac`, `apc_frac` | 0.074, 0.066 | Parameters.csv `Tc_frac`, `APC_frac` |
| `vcell` | 1e-6 mm^3/cell | Parameters.csv `Vcell` |
| `ksyn_apc_tme` | 108005.973888231 cells/mL/day | Parameters.csv `ksyn_APC_tme` |
| `apc_syn_scale` | 5000 | Reactions.csv `v4` rate law |
| `kdeath_apc_tme`, `kdeath_apc_ln` | 0.0466 1/day | Parameters.csv `beta_APC_tme`, `beta_APC_ln` |
| `qlymph` (L) | 7.03 L/day | Parameters.csv `L`; Assignments.csv A14 |
| `apc_ln0` | 1e6 cells | Species.csv `APC_ln` initial state |
| `kpro_tc_ln` (Pro_Tc_ln) | 1.5 1/day | Parameters.csv `Pro_Tc_ln`; Assignments.csv A21 |
| `kdeath_tc_ln`, `kdeath_tc_tme` | 0.0014 1/day | Parameters.csv `beta_Tc_ln`, `beta_Tc_tme` |
| `qco` (Q), `vplasma` (P) | 4730 L/day, 5 L | Parameters.csv `Q`, `P`; Assignments.csv A15 |
| `tc_ln0` | 137554.400017073 cells | Species.csv `Tc_ln` initial state |
| `tumor_max`, `tc_max`, `apc_max` | derived | Assignments.csv A22-A27 |
| Initial states of `tumor`, `capacity`, `tc_tme`, `apc_tme` | derived from `TUM_VOL` | Assignments.csv A4, A8, A10; initialiseQSP.R |
| TME volume and percentages | algebraic | Compartments.csv `TME`; Assignments.csv A2, A6, A11, A13 |
| Rate laws and ODEs | -- | Reactions.csv; integrateQSP.R `odeRateStepQSP` |
| Dose 4794.521 nmol every 504 h, 19 doses | -- | DosingPlans.csv; doseEventQSP.R |
| Virtual-trial distributions | -- | Supplementary Information, "Parameters varied in virtual trial simulation"; Assignments.csv A1, A3, A5, A16-A21 |

The maintainers checked the packaged model against the authors' R export
(`simulateIndividualQSP()` with deSolve `vode`) on 2026-11-27 for one
non-nominal parameter set (initial volume 5000 mm^3, all six varied rate
constants and both TME fractions moved off their nominal values, 19 doses):
tumour volume and all seven immune/tumour states agreed to a relative
difference below 1e-9 at all 209 output times, and the plasma concentration
to below 1e-5.

# Dosing and helpers

```{r helpers}
mw_pembro <- 146000 # g/mol
dose_nmol <- 10 * 70 / mw_pembro * 1e6 # 10 mg/kg at 70 kg = 700 mg
dose_nmol
dose_days <- seq(0, 378, by = 21) # 19 doses, Q3W
obs_days <- seq(0, 398, by = 2)

make_events <- function(ids, treated) {
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_days) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  if (treated) {
    dose <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = dose_days) |>
      mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "depot")
    obs <- bind_rows(dose, obs)
  }
  arrange(obs, id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

# Typical patient

With the nominal parameters and the nominal initial tumour volume (12592.5
mm^3, the day-0 size of calibration patient 1130), the untreated tumour grows
roughly 25-fold over 398 days. Under pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W it first
shrinks by about a third (day 100) and then escapes, ending near twice its
starting volume; the virtual population below shows the spread around this
nominal patient.

```{r typical}
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  make_events(1, treated = FALSE) |> mutate(arm = "Untreated"),
  make_events(2, treated = TRUE) |> mutate(arm = "Pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W")
) |>
  mutate(TUM_VOL = 12592.53909)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, typ_events, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")

typ_comp <- typ |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  transmute(arm, tumor_vol, pct_tumor, pct_tc, pct_apc, total = pct_tumor + pct_tc + pct_apc)
knitr::kable(typ_comp, digits = 3)
```

```{r typical-checks}
stopifnot(
  # The tumour starts at TUM_VOL with the TME at its maximal leukocyte
  # fractions (86 / 7.4 / 6.6 %) -- a check of the initial-state algebra.
  all(abs(typ_comp$tumor_vol / 12592.53909 - 1) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(typ_comp$total - 100) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(typ_comp$pct_tc - 7.4) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(typ_comp$pct_apc - 6.6) < 1e-10)
)
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical-patient tumour volume, untreated and treated (nominal parameters)."}
ggplot(typ, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumour volume (mm^3)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Virtual trial (Figure 4)

The virtual population follows the authors' deposited code. Six rate
constants are drawn uniformly between half and the full nominal value, the
initial tumour volume uniformly between 10 and 10000 mm^3, and the relative
cytotoxic T-cell and APC fractions from log-normal distributions. The
log-normal draws reproduce the deposited code's conversion exactly (see
Assumptions and deviations). The cohort is 200 virtual patients rather than
the paper's 489; each patient is simulated both untreated and treated.

```{r vp}
set.seed(20200213)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20200213)
n_vp <- 200
lnorm_code <- function(n, m, s) {
  rlnorm(n, log(m^2 / sqrt(s^2 + m^2)), sqrt(log(s^2 / m^2 + 1)))
}
vp <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_vp),
  TUM_VOL = runif(n_vp, 0.01, 10) * 1000,
  kg_tumor = runif(n_vp, 0.2, 0.4),
  kv1 = runif(n_vp, 0.005, 0.01),
  kdeath_tumor = runif(n_vp, 0.01155, 0.0231),
  kkill = runif(n_vp, 0.15, 0.3),
  kexh_pd1 = runif(n_vp, 150, 300),
  kpro_tc_ln = runif(n_vp, 0.75, 1.5),
  tc_frac = lnorm_code(n_vp, -2.436, 0.62335),
  apc_frac = lnorm_code(n_vp, -2.58098, 0.69689)
)

run_arm <- function(treated, label) {
  # Per-patient values travel as data columns, which override the ini()
  # values of the same name.
  ev <- make_events(vp$id, treated) |>
    left_join(vp, by = "id")
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(arm = label)
}
sim_vp <- bind_rows(
  run_arm(FALSE, "Untreated"),
  run_arm(TRUE, "Pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W")
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = c("Untreated", "Pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W")))
```

The four calibration patients' tumour volumes (KEYNOTE-001, digitised by the
authors from Chatterjee et al. 2016 and deposited with the model code as
`Chatterjee_etal_2016_10mgperkg_TGI.csv`) are overlaid as in Figure 4A-B.

```{r clinical}
clin <- data.frame(
  ID = rep(c(1125, 1130, 946, 609), times = c(5, 5, 7, 6)),
  time = c(
    0, 63.47, 126.94, 183.94, 252.59,
    0, 63.16, 130.26, 194.74, 256.58,
    0, 66.34, 126.83, 191.22, 253.66, 318.05, 378.54,
    0, 69.35, 132.66, 195.98, 266.83, 293.97
  ),
  tumor_vol = c(
    21119.86043, 23139.34957, 6226.313456, 3267.081646, 3761.256671,
    12592.53909, 1932.883374, 220.8932335, 241.3760003, 241.3760003,
    13042.78256, 9710.921562, 7728.429809, 7728.429809, 8504.464731, 14137.16694, 12345.5062,
    16217.91484, 17326.73148, 34847.18435, 34847.18435, 91780.0197, 95267.17819
  )
)
```

```{r fig4ab, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4A-B of Lazarou 2020: tumour volume of 200 virtual patients (blue) untreated and treated with pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W, with the four KEYNOTE-001 calibration patients (red; patient 609 did not respond)."}
ggplot(sim_vp, aes(time, tumor_vol)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = id), colour = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = clin, aes(group = ID), colour = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = clin, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1e5)) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Tumour volume (mm^3)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper's waterfall plot (Figure 4C) shows the percent change from baseline
at the end of the simulation for each treated virtual patient, after removing
those whose tumour more than doubled (the deposited code drops every patient
with an absolute change above 100 %). The paper reports a dropout of 35 %.

```{r waterfall}
final <- sim_vp |>
  filter(arm == "Pembrolizumab 10 mg/kg Q3W", time == max(obs_days)) |>
  select(id, pct_change)
dropout_pct <- 100 * mean(abs(final$pct_change) > 100)
kept <- final |>
  filter(abs(pct_change) <= 100) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_change)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())
dropout_pct
```

```{r fig4c, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4C of Lazarou 2020: waterfall plot of the percent change in tumour volume from baseline at day 398 for treated virtual patients whose tumour did not double."}
ggplot(kept, aes(rank, pct_change)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-100, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Virtual patient", y = "% change from baseline") +
  theme_bw()
```

In this cohort `r round(dropout_pct)` % of treated virtual patients more than
double their tumour volume by day 398, against 35 % in the paper.

```{r waterfall-checks}
stopifnot(
  # The share of treated virtual patients whose tumour doubles lands near the
  # paper's 35 %: a wrong growth, kill or exhaustion term moves it by far more
  # than the +/-15 point allowance, which covers cohort sampling noise
  # (binomial SE about 3.4 points at n = 200).
  abs(dropout_pct - 35) < 15
)
```

```{r arm-summary}
sim_vp |>
  filter(time == max(obs_days)) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct_change = median(pct_change),
    pct_shrinking = 100 * mean(pct_change < 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Pembrolizumab PK (PKNCA)

The paper reports no NCA results. The PK layer is checked against its own
mass balance: after a single dose, the area under the plasma concentration
curve must equal `fdepot * dose / kel` converted to concentration units, and
the terminal half-life must equal `log(2)` over the slow disposition
eigenvalue of the two-compartment system.

```{r pk-sim}
pk_events <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, seq(0.25, 7, by = 0.25), seq(8, 400, by = 2)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central"),
  data.frame(id = 2L, time = dose_days, evid = 1L, amt = dose_nmol, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 2L, time = c(0, 357 + seq(0, 21, by = 0.25)), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = ifelse(id == 1L, "Single dose", "Dose 18 of Q3W"),
    TUM_VOL = 1000
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, pk_events, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
```

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time = ifelse(treatment == "Dose 18 of Q3W", time - 357, time)) |>
  filter(time >= 0)
dose_df <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1L, (id == 1L) | (time == 357)) |>
  mutate(time = ifelse(id == 2L, 0, time), amt_mg = amt * mw_pembro / 1e6) |>
  select(id, time, amt_mg, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt_mg ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = c(Inf, 21),
  treatment = c("Single dose", "Dose 18 of Q3W"),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life", "auclast", "cmin")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
knitr::kable(nca_tab, digits = 2)
```

```{r pk-checks}
k12 <- 0.4
k21 <- 0.43
kel <- 0.07342571
sum_k <- k12 + k21 + kel
beta <- (sum_k - sqrt(sum_k^2 - 4 * k21 * kel)) / 2
auc_expected <- 0.9815751 * dose_nmol / kel * mw_pembro / 2.75 * 1e-6
nca_val <- function(test, trt) {
  nca_tab$PPORRES[nca_tab$PPTESTCD == test & nca_tab$treatment == trt]
}
c(
  aucinf_pknca = nca_val("aucinf.obs", "Single dose"),
  aucinf_mass_balance = auc_expected,
  thalf_pknca = nca_val("half.life", "Single dose"),
  thalf_eigenvalue = log(2) / beta
)
stopifnot(
  # Closed-form checks of the deterministic PK layer (same parameters on
  # both sides), so tight tolerances are appropriate.
  abs(nca_val("aucinf.obs", "Single dose") / auc_expected - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(nca_val("half.life", "Single dose") / (log(2) / beta) - 1) < 0.01
)
```

The terminal half-life implied by the authors' rate constants is about 19
days. The 10 mg/kg peak is about 165 ug/mL after the first dose and about
270 ug/mL at steady state, with a steady-state trough of about 105 ug/mL;
these follow from the 2.75 L volume the model uses to convert amount to
concentration.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Model-code version.** The Supplementary Information text names the code
  archive `CIC_v2.2.5`, but the deposited archive is `CIC_v2.2.6` (R and
  MATLAB exports dated 20 December 2019). The packaged model follows the
  deposited v2.2.6 code, which is what produced Figure 4.
* **Initial lymph-node T cells.** The Supplementary Information text derives
  195,624 pre-existing neoantigen-specific cytotoxic T cells in the lymph node,
  but the deposited code (`Species.csv`, `initialiseQSP.R`) starts `Tc_ln` at
  137,554.4 cells. The code value is used, as it is what the authors ran.
* **Log-normal TME fractions.** The Supplementary Information describes the
  relative cytotoxic T-cell and APC fractions as log-normal with "mean"
  -2.436 / -2.58098 and "SD" 0.62335 / 0.69689 -- values that read as the
  mean and SD of the log. The deposited R and MATLAB code instead pass them to
  a conversion that treats them as the arithmetic mean and SD of the
  log-normal variable (`log(m^2 / sqrt(s^2 + m^2))`,
  `sqrt(log(s^2 / m^2 + 1))`). Because only the ratio of the two fractions
  enters the model, the code's convention gives a median T-cell : APC ratio
  of about 0.95 with a narrow spread, whereas the log-scale reading would give
  about 1.16 with a wider spread. The vignette follows the code, which
  generated Figure 4; `ini()` carries the nominal fractions 0.074 and 0.066
  either way.
* **Untreated patients.** The deposited code simulates untreated patients by
  still dosing but setting a switch `doseOn = 0` that multiplies the drug
  amount seen by the PD-1 term. The packaged model omits the switch; an
  untreated patient is simulated with no doses, which gives an identical
  tumour response.
* **Injection-site depot.** Pembrolizumab is given by intravenous infusion,
  but the authors' PK model (fitted to a Simcyp simulation) doses into an
  injection-site compartment with first-order absorption (`kabs` = 2/day) and
  a non-absorbed fraction. This structure is kept as published; doses go into
  `depot`.
* **Amount-based affinity.** PD-1 occupancy is computed from the central
  amount and a dissociation constant expressed as an amount (0.0766 nmol), as
  in the deposited code, not from a concentration.
* **Constant in the APC development rate.** The rate law multiplies
  `ksyn_APC_tme` by a bare 5000 (commented "blood volume = 5 L"). It is
  carried as the fixed parameter `apc_syn_scale` so the value is visible.
* **Units.** The deposited R code works internally in cubic metres, moles and
  days. The packaged model keeps days, expresses the drug in nmol, tumour
  volume in mm^3 and concentration in ug/mL, and converts the TME volume
  explicitly where the source parameter is per mL (`ksyn_apc_tme`) or per
  litre (`qlymph`).
* **Initial tumour volume as a covariate.** The source parameter
  `Initial_tumor_volume` is supplied per patient through the `TUM_VOL`
  column (mm^3); it is only an initial condition and the reference of the
  percent change from baseline.
* **No variability or residual error.** The model is deterministic. The
  virtual-trial distributions are uniform and log-normal draws of fixed
  parameters, which the vignette reproduces with `rxSolve(params = ...)`
  rather than as random effects.
* **Cohort size.** The vignette simulates 200 virtual patients per arm
  instead of the paper's 489, and the virtual population differs from the
  paper's because it uses different random numbers (the authors note that
  their own code gives "similar but not identical" results on each run).
